You have Atlassian MCP tools available but DEFERRED. First run ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__mcp-atlassian__confluence_get_page" and max_results 2 to load the schema.

Then read these two Confluence pages IN FULL (convert_to_markdown=true, include_metadata=true):
1. Page ID 303071234 — "04.1.1 Homepage and Content" (Req ID prefix HPC)
2. Page ID 303890433 — "04.1.17 Third Party Integrations"

Context: I am researching the CONSENT position for a "Recently Viewed products" feature (stores a shopper's product browsing history — session-only for guests, account-persisted for logged-in shoppers) on the Zimmermann SFCC PWA storefront.

For EACH page report:
- The page's version number (from metadata) and any "last updated" / "extracted on" date stated in the body text.
- EVERY requirement row (quote the Req ID where present + the full requirement text verbatim) that relates to ANY of: consent, cookies, Didomi, GDPR/CCPA/privacy, tracking, personalisation, browsing history, recently viewed, data retention, or per-storefront consent defaults. Include Owner / Storefront / Status / Comments column values for those rows.
- Both pages are known to have a consent section ("Consent & Cookie Management" on 04.1.1; "Consent and Privacy" on 04.1.17) — reproduce those sections completely and verbatim.
- Explicitly state whether either page mentions "Recently Viewed" at all, whether either states any DATA RETENTION PERIOD, and whether either distinguishes guest vs logged-in/authenticated treatment.
- Note any per-region differences (AU vs EU/UK vs US vs HK/ME).
- Note anything about which Didomi purpose/category names or purpose IDs are used.

Be exhaustive and quote verbatim. Do NOT modify anything — read-only. Do not write any files. Return findings as your final message.

Read-only research complete. Both pages read in full (markdown + raw storage format cross-checked; nothing modified).

# Page 1 — 04.1.1 Homepage and Content (ID 303071234)

**Version: 14.** URL: https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/303071234

**Date stated in body (verbatim):**
> "Requirements extracted from Zimmermann Functional Requirements excel, downloaded July 3rd, 2026 after all requirements were confirmed. — source of truth. Req ID prefix: **HPC**."

Second body line:
> "⚠️ **Rows with strikethrough are out of scope** — struck through in the Excel source file."

The MCP tool returned empty `created`/`updated` timestamps, so version 14 + the 3 July 2026 extraction date are the only dating available.

**Column set (important — there is no Owner and no Storefront column on this page):** `Req ID | Functional Area | Sub-Functional Area | Requirement | Status | Comments | User Stories`. 40 data rows, **all 40 with Status = "Confirmed"**.

**Strikethrough check:** I searched the raw storage format for `<s>`, `</s>`, `<del`, `<strike`, `line-through` — **zero occurrences**. No row on this page is out of scope; the ⚠️ note is inert here.

## "Consent & Cookie Management" section — reproduced completely and verbatim

The Sub-Functional Area "Consent & Cookie Management" contains **exactly two rows**:

| Req ID | Functional Area | Sub-Functional Area | Requirement | Status | Comments |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| HPC-013 | Homepage & Content | Consent & Cookie Management | "The system should grey out all site content and prevent interaction with all site elements when the Didomi consent notice is displayed." | Confirmed | *(empty)* |
| HPC-014 | Homepage & Content | Consent & Cookie Management | "The system should remove the grey out effect and restore full site interactivity once the customer has completed the Didomi consent flow." | Confirmed | *(empty)* |

User Stories links: `...labels%3DPRD-013` and `...labels%3DPRD-014` respectively.

**That is the entire consent section.** It is purely about the *visual blocking behaviour* of the banner. It says nothing about cookie categories, purposes, storage, defaults, or what may/may not be written before consent.

## Every other row touching consent / privacy / persistence / auth state

| Req ID | Sub-Functional Area | Requirement (verbatim) | Status | Comments (verbatim) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| HPC-040 | Chat Integration | "The system should only initialise the chat widget after the customer has consented to the relevant cookie category via Didomi." | Confirmed | *(empty)* |
| HPC-037 | Navigation — Footer | "The system should display appropriate privacy consent copy and a link to the local Privacy Policy on the sign-up modal." | Confirmed | "Additional Note: Should display Accessibility  @Jasmijn Tsang" |
| HPC-027 | Navigation — Header | "The system should persist the customer's selected region across sessions." | Confirmed | *(empty)* |
| HPC-026 | Navigation — Header | "The system should display a country/region selector in the header to allow customers to switch locale and country excluding the AU store." | Confirmed | *(empty)* |
| HPC-019 | Navigation — Header | "The system should display a Wishlist icon that navigates anonymous customers to the login page." | Confirmed | *(empty)* |
| HPC-020 | Navigation — Header | "The system should display a Wishlist icon that navigates logged in customers to the wishlist page." | Confirmed | *(empty)* |
| HPC-036 | Navigation — Footer | "The system should pass email sign-up data to Omneo (who will then pass to Emarsys)" | Confirmed | *(empty)* |
| HPC-038 | Navigation — Footer | "The system should allow business users to add region specific footer links (e.g Acknowledgement of Country for AU storefront)." | Confirmed | *(empty)* |
| *(blank Req ID)* | Chat Integration | "The system should display the chat widget as a pop-up overlay on the relevant pages. Page visibility rules are determined by Inside Chat." | Confirmed | *(empty)* |

**Two source-data anomalies worth flagging:**
- HPC-008's Req ID cell literally contains `/HPC-008` (leading slash) in the stored content — a source typo, not a conversion artefact. I verified this in the raw HTML.
- The chat-widget row sitting between HPC-038 and HPC-040 has a **genuinely empty Req ID cell** (` `). By sequence and by its own Jira link (`labels=PRD-039`) it is **HPC-039**, but the ID is missing from the page.

## Keyword scan of page 1 (raw text, case-insensitive)

Zero occurrences: `recently viewed`, `recently`, `viewed`, `retention`, `retain`, `guest`, `browsing`, `history`, `personalis*`, `personaliz*`, `recommend`, `GDPR`, `CCPA`, `track*`, `opt-in` / `opt in`, `local storage` / `localStorage`.

Present: `consent` ×6, `cookie` ×3, `Didomi` ×3, `privacy` ×2, `wishlist` ×3, `anonymous` ×1 (HPC-019), `logged in` ×1 (HPC-020), `session` ×1 (HPC-027 "across sessions").

# Direct answers to your five explicit questions

**1. Does either page mention "Recently Viewed"?**
**No. Neither page mentions it at all** — not "recently viewed", not "recently", not "viewed", not "browsing history", not "browse history". Verified by raw-text scan on both. There is no requirement ID anywhere on 04.1.1 that a Recently Viewed feature could be traced to.

**2. Does either page state a DATA RETENTION PERIOD?**
**No. Neither page states any retention period, TTL, expiry, or purge rule for anything** — not for consent preferences, not for the persisted region selection (HPC-027 says only "across sessions"), not for cookies, not for any stored customer data. Zero hits for `retention` / `retain` / `expiry` / `days` on either page.

**3. Does either page distinguish guest vs logged-in / authenticated treatment?**
**Only incidentally, and never in a consent or data-storage context.**
- 04.1.1 distinguishes them exactly once, for the **Wishlist icon destination only**: HPC-019 (anonymous → login page) vs HPC-020 (logged in → wishlist page). That is a navigation rule, not a storage or consent rule.
- 04.1.17 mentions "authenticated state" once, and only as a **data-layer attribute Crazy Egg needs**.
- **Neither page states any differential consent, storage or persistence treatment between guest and logged-in shoppers.** Your session-only-for-guests / account-persisted-for-logged-in split has no requirement backing on either page, in either direction.

**4. Per-region differences (AU vs EU/UK vs US vs HK/ME)?**
**No per-region consent differences are stated on either page.** In fact 04.1.17 states the opposite of regional variation for the banner: "presenting a cookie consent banner on first visit **across all storefronts**". The regional distinctions that *do* appear are non-consent:
- HPC-026 — region selector in header "**excluding the AU store**".
- HPC-038 — region-specific footer links, "e.g Acknowledgement of Country for **AU** storefront".
- HPC-037 — "a link to the **local** Privacy Policy" (implies per-region policy documents, but does not state their content or any differing consent default).
- HPC-005 / HPC-007 / HPC-011 — locale-specific and global-vs-localised content model (policy pages named as localised).
- 04.1.17 Global-e — "**HK, ME, US international and EU international** storefronts" own their checkout/payment/tax.
- 04.1.17 Klarna — "**AU and US** storefronts". Avalara — "US domestic, New Zealand and New Caledonia and EU domestic".
- Note: the US pre-checked marketing opt-in rule that lives in AGENTS.md / `.docs/prd/regional.md` is **not** on either of these pages.

**5. Didomi purpose / category names or purpose IDs?**
**Neither page names a single Didomi purpose, category, or purpose ID.** The closest either gets is HPC-040's unnamed placeholder: "after the customer has consented to **the relevant cookie category**". 04.1.17 explains why the taxonomy is absent: "**Didomi configuration and tag-layer gating are out of scope for SFCC and remain with Zimmermann.**" The purpose/category vocabulary is owned outside this repo and outside these PRDs.

---

# What this means for the Recently Viewed consent position

- **There is no requirement to cite.** Neither page authorises, prohibits, or scopes a browsing-history feature. Under AGENTS.md's Requirements rule ("If a requirement is missing, ambiguous, or not yet confirmed — stop, flag the ambiguity, propose a solution, and wait for user approval"), this is a genuine missing-requirement stop, not a gap to fill by inference.
- **The only stated consent gate is narrower than you may need.** 04.1.17 gates "**Third-party tracking and marketing scripts**". Recently Viewed as *first-party* session storage or an *account-persisted* attribute is not a third-party script — so that sentence neither permits nor forbids it. This is the precise crux of the question and both pages are silent on it.
- **The one feature-level consent-gating precedent on either page is HPC-040** (chat widget gated on "the relevant cookie category via Didomi"). If a gating pattern is wanted for Recently Viewed, HPC-040 is the shape to mirror — but its category is unnamed there too, so mirroring it still leaves the purpose ID unresolved.
- **Einstein is named as the owner of "all search, merchandising and product recommendation functionality across all storefronts."** If Recently Viewed is built as an Einstein recommender rather than local storage, it inherits Einstein's consent posture — which neither page states.
- **Two open items you will have to source elsewhere:** the Didomi purpose taxonomy (owned by Zimmermann per 04.1.17, not in these PRDs — likely `.docs/prd/regional.md` or the Didomi console), and any retention period (absent from both pages entirely).
